Liam to share SCIM attribute mapping doc

Schedule pilot SSO + SCIM test on staging (week of 10/20)

summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Skyline Bank security team through SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege model. Discussed audit logging, KMS encryption, data residency, and SOC2/ISO artifacts. Agreed next steps to exchange metadata, run a staging pilot, and provide policy templates.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-13
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Aisha (CISO - Skyline), Robert (Dir Identity), Nora (Security Eng)

Topics: SSO/SAML flow, SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency, SOC2/ISO certs

00:00 - Maya: Okay everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'll hand it to Liam to run through the technical flow then we'll get into RBAC.
00:18 - Liam: Great, hi, I'm Liam, Redwood solutions engineer. Quick agenda: SAML SP setup, SCIM provisioning for users/groups, RBAC/least-privilege mapping, audit logs and encryption at rest.
00:36 - Aisha: Hi, thanks. Our main concerns are account provisioning accuracy and ensuring we don't overprovision privileges. Also we need audit logs that meet internal retention and our auditors.
00:50 - Robert: We use Okta currently as our IDP, we may evaluate Ping for some BUs. We're interested in SCIM auto-provisioning and group sync.
01:05 - Liam: Ok -- Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SP metadata; we can provide ACS endpoints, entity ID, certs. For SCIM we support standard /Users and /Groups endpoints and mapping of attributes.
01:22 - Nora: What about SCIM rate limits? We've had issues with big syncs at another vendor.
01:35 - Liam: Good question. We have a throttle; our SCIM service processes in batches, default 60 reqs/min but it's configurable for Dedicated customers. For hosted there are per-tenant caps, we can raise for pilot.
01:55 - Maya: To add, we'll share a SCIM mapping spreadsheet that shows default attribute mappings (email, displayName, roles) and notes on custom extensions.
02:10 - Aisha: On RBAC, show us how we'd do least-privilege. We want to ensure ops can't see PII, only certain audit roles can pull logs.
02:24 - Liam: Our RBAC model supports role definitions and resource scoping. You can create roles like 'AuditReader' with read-only access to logs, 'ModelOperator' scoped to specific model endpoints, and 'BillingViewer' for cost only.
02:40 - Robert: How granular are the resource scopes? Can we limit to a project or route?
02:50 - Liam: Yes, scopes are by project, environment (prod/stage), and model route. There is also attribute-based access tied to SAML assertions if you want group-to-role mapping.
03:05 - (brief crosstalk)
03:20 - Nora: We want automated provisioning, but also manual overrides. For example contractors should be time-limited access. Does SCIM support expiration?
03:35 - Liam: SCIM itself doesn't do TTL natively, but our platform supports a 'provisioning policy' layer - you can mark accounts as provisioned_by_scim and set expiry dates; we also emit events to your audit log.
03:50 - Maya: We'll include a doc on recommended lifecycle policies for contractors.
04:05 - Aisha: Encryption at rest — do you integrate with our KMS? We have a bank-managed HSM and strict key custody rules.
04:18 - Liam: Redwood supports external KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted, we offer Redwood-managed KMS but we can discuss Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) where keys are in a customer KMS — note: that requires Dedicated or Private.
04:36 - Robert: So hosted won't meet our HSM requirement?
04:42 - Liam: Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys in AWS KMS; if you need HSM-backed keys under your control, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
04:55 - Nora: Audit logs — retention and schema? Auditors want immutable logs and export capability.
05:06 - Liam: We produce structured audit events: auth events, SCIM provisioning events, admin role changes, model access, and request-level metadata. Retention is configurable; for enterprise contracts we support longer retention and offload to S3 or your SIEM via streaming.
05:25 - Aisha: Do logs include token-level redaction? We can't have API keys logged in plaintext.
05:34 - Liam: Sensitive fields are masked by default; full raw payloads can be sent to a secure archive if required.
05:44 - Maya: We'll attach a sample events schema and how to connect to your SIEM.
06:00 - (interruption) Speaker 1: Sorry, quick question on SAML group mapping...
06:08 - Liam: Yes, group-to-role mapping is done via SAML attributes or SCIM group sync. For Okta, we recommend sending the group claim with the role mapping, and then Redwood maps groups to roles automatically.
06:25 - Robert: We're worried about drift if groups in Okta are large. Can we do a sync dry-run?
06:34 - Liam: We have a staging sync mode that runs in dry-run and outputs a delta report — shows adds/removes. We'll provide that for the pilot.
06:48 - Nora: Does Redwood support SCIM 2.0 extension for enterprise user schema? We have custom attributes like employeeType, costCenter.
06:58 - Liam: Yes, custom attributes are supported; just add them in the mapping spreadsheet and we can persist as user metadata. Be aware some nested attributes sometimes get flattened in transcripts — sorry, bad example — sometimes SCIM payloads need transformation.
07:18 - Aisha: SOC2 and ISO — can you share your latest certs? Our procurement requires SOC2 Type II evidence and ISO 27001 scope.
07:28 - Maya: Absolutely. We'll share a redacted SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate and a security whitepaper that covers scope and controls.
07:40 - Aisha: Data residency — our production data must remain in US East for now. How do you handle region pinning?
07:50 - Liam: We support region pinning for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can select region preference and we route accordingly but it's not strict residency guarantee unless under Dedicated contract.
08:05 - Robert: For the pilot, we need all data remain in US-East. Is that doable?
08:12 - Liam: For the staging pilot we can provision a Dedicated staging instance or a VPC-backed private test instance to ensure residency. We'll confirm costs.
08:25 - (longer section, 08:25-20:00 omitted for brevity in this transcript export)
20:05 - Aisha: Let's talk SAML setup specifics. We'll be using Okta; what do you need from us?
20:15 - Liam: We need your IdP metadata XML or the federation endpoints, x509 cert for signing, and attribute names you will send (email, name, groups). We will provide SP metadata: ACS URL, entity ID, and the certificate we want signed assertions or encrypted responses?
20:33 - Robert: We prefer signed assertions, encrypted optional. Are encrypted assertions supported?
20:40 - Liam: We support encrypted assertions; we'll need your public key. For initial pilot signed assertions is fine and simpler.
20:52 - Nora: For provisioning, will SCIM be push from Okta or do you call Redwood SCIM endpoint?
21:00 - Liam: Okta is typically configured to push to our SCIM endpoint. We'll hand you the base URL and bearer token. Okta supports scheduled sync and on-demand provisioning.
21:14 - Maya: We'll send a short checklist for Okta admin to configure SAML app and SCIM integration, including sample mappings and troubleshooting tips.
21:26 - Aisha: On RBAC examples, can you show a recommended least-privilege role matrix?
21:34 - Liam: Sure. Example roles: Admin (full), AuditReader (logs only), ModelDeployer (deploy only to specific model routes), SupportAgent (read-only on routes plus ability to debug), Billing (costs & invoices). We can provide JSON templates you can import via API.
21:54 - Robert: JSON templates good — will they include conditionals like time-limited access?
22:01 - Liam: We support role bindings with expiration timestamps; you can create temporary membership entries. For contractors, tie to SCIM 'employeeType' or an Okta group that you rotate.
22:18 - Maya: Also note we have SSO session timeouts and you can enforce idle timeouts centrally via SAML sessions.
22:30 - Nora: Auditing of admin changes — do you keep who changed role bindings?
22:38 - Liam: Yes, admin audit events include actor, timestamp, previous and new state, and we keep immutable logs for compliance.
22:48 - Aisha: About encryption: you said BYOK requires Dedicated/Private. Can you walk through key rotation and split custody?
22:58 - Liam: For BYOK we support key import from your KMS or integrate with AWS KMS/CloudHSM. Keys can be set to rotate; we support manual rotation and scheduled rotation. For split custody, it's more an organizational control but we support HSM-backed keys where the customer retains admin privileges over the KMS.
23:20 - Robert: Does log export to S3 encrypt with our key?
23:27 - Liam: Yes, if you're using our offload we can encrypt S3 objects with your KMS key (SSE-KMS) and restrict access to the bucket.
23:35 - (brief pause)
23:45 - Maya: Quick note — some transcripts earlier mention 'KV cache' and 'KV' which is different from KMS — sorry for jargon confusion.
23:55 - Nora: Haha, yes please keep KV cache and KMS distinct.
24:05 - Liam: We'll include a glossary in the doc pack.
24:15 - Maya: Next on the agenda — emergency access and break glass. Do you have a documented break glass process?
24:25 - Liam: Yes, break glass is supported with dedicated workflows: time-limited elevated access that requires justification and is recorded in audit logs and triggers alerts. For Dedicated we can hook to your ticketing system for approvals.
24:40 - Aisha: Good. For compliance, can we run a pen-test or do you have a third-party assessment?
24:50 - Maya: We do annual third-party pen tests and can provide an executive summary and remediation timeline. For customers wanting to run their own, we have a test plan we ask to follow and a timeline to schedule.
25:05 - (discussion continues, slightly messy transcription with filler words)
30:12 - Robert: Can we get a sample RBAC JSON and a sample SAML metadata?
30:18 - Maya: Yes, will attach examples.
30:24 - Nora: Is there an API to manage roles and bindings?
30:28 - Liam: Yes, full Admin API for role management, user management, and SCIM connectors. We'll provide rate limits and example cURL and SDK commands.
30:40 - Aisha: Any multi-factor/authn requirements? We require MFA for admin roles.
30:47 - Liam: We honor the IdP MFA. We also support conditional access via SAML attributes and can require step-up auth for sensitive routes.
30:58 - Maya: We'll also include our guidance on session durations and MFA enforcement best practices.
31:08 - (noise, small cross-talk)
31:30 - Nora: One last question on retention — auditors require 7 years for certain logs. Is that feasible?
31:38 - Liam: On Dedicated we can support arbitrary retention by offloading to your S3 or archive. Hosted has constraints but enterprise contracts can extend retention. We'll include options and an estimated cost delta.
31:55 - Aisha: Perfect. Let's recap actions.
32:05 - Maya: Recap: we'll send SP metadata, SCIM mapping doc, RBAC templates, SOC2/ISO certs, and schedule a staging pilot.
32:18 - Robert: Skyline will provide Okta test tenant and a list of sample users/groups to test.
32:25 - Nora: I'll provision the test IDP lab account and share metadata.
32:30 - Maya: Great. Any blockers for the week of 10/20 pilot?
32:36 - Aisha: None immediate, procurement will need the SOC2 docs but that's fine.
32:42 - Maya: Okay we'll follow up via email with the pack. Thanks everyone.
52:00 - Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'skim' for SCIM, 'kay em ess' for KMS). Several references to shared artifacts: (link) SCIM mapping spreadsheet, (link) SAML quickstart, (link) RBAC JSON templates, (link) SOC2 summary.
